arxiv-2011-09151.title: Triadic resonances driven by thermal convection in a rotating sphere
arxiv-2011-09151.creator: Yufeng Lin 1
arxiv-2011-09151.description: Abstract We report for the first time on triadic resonances in a rotating convection system. Using direct numerical simulations, we find that convective modes in a rotating spherical fluid can excite a pair of inertial modes whose frequencies and wavenumbers match the triadic resonance conditions.

arxiv-2111-08799.title: DeltaConv: Anisotropic Operators for Geometric Deep Learning on Point Clouds Journal: TOG Volume: 41 4 105 7 DOI: 10.1145/3528223.3530166 CCS: Computing methodologies Neural networks CCS: Computing methodologies Shape analysis
arxiv-2111-08799.creator: Ruben Wiersma, Ahmad Nasikun, Elmar Eisemann, Klaus Hildebrandt
arxiv-2111-08799.description: Abstract . Learning from 3D point-cloud data has rapidly gained momentum, motivated by the success of deep learning on images and the increased availability of 3D data. In this paper, we aim to construct anisotropic convolution layers that work directly on the surface derived from a point cloud.

arxiv-2305-17013.title: D-CALM : A Dynamic Clustering-based Active Learning Approach for Mitigating Bias
arxiv-2305-17013.creator: Sabit Hassan, Malihe Alikhani
arxiv-2305-17013.description: Abstract Despite recent advancements, NLP models continue to be vulnerable to bias. This bias often originates from the uneven distribution of real-world data and can propagate through the annotation process. Escalated integration of these models in our lives calls for methods to mitigate bias without overbearing annotation costs.

arxiv-2503-01832.title: Rotary Outliers and Rotary Offset Features in Large Language Models
arxiv-2503-01832.creator: André Jonasson
arxiv-2503-01832.description: Abstract Transformer-based Large Language Models (LLMs) rely on positional encodings to provide sequence position information to their attention mechanism. Rotary Positional Encodings (RoPE), which encode relative position by rotating queries and keys, have become widely used in modern LLMs. We study the features and patterns that emerge in queries and keys when using rotary embeddings.

arxiv-2504-16109.title: Representation Learning for Tabular Data: A Comprehensive Survey
arxiv-2504-16109.creator: Jun-Peng Jiang, Si-Yang Liu, Hao-Run Cai, Qile Zhou, Han-Jia Ye
arxiv-2504-16109.description: Abstract Tabular data, structured as rows and columns, is among the most prevalent data types in machine learning classification and regression applications. Models for learning from tabular data have continuously evolved, with Deep Neural Networks (DNNs) recently demonstrating promising results through their capability of representation learning.

pmc-10615161.title: Intersecting epidemics: COVID-19 and HIV in sub-Saharan Africa. A systematic review (2020-2022)
pmc-10615161.creator: TALENT TAPERA, CLIFFORD ODIMEGWU, REBAONE PETLELE, MATSHIDISO VALERIA SELLO, ARMSTRONG DZOMBA, OLUWATOYIN ALADEJEBI, MILLION PHIRI
pmc-10615161.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2023). There has been significant progress with regards to winning the fight against HIV globally, particularly due to the introduction of antiretroviral therapy (ART). COVID-19 threatened to derail gains in the fight against HIV. As we have started to see with studies on COVID-19 and HIV, there is a need to ‘provide an in-depth view’ in understanding the dynamics between the two epidemics, especially in sub-Saharan Africa.

pmc-10649681.title: Patient Position in Operative Endoscopy
pmc-10649681.creator: Lino Polese, Emilia Giugliano, Michele Valmasoni, Toshio Uraoka, Jun Kato
pmc-10649681.description: It is well known by surgeons that patient positioning is fundamental to exposing the organs when performing an operation via laparoscopy, as gravity can help move the organs and facilitate the exposure of the surgical site. But is it also important for endoscopic procedures? This paper examines various types of endoscopic operations and addresses the issue of the patient’s position.

pmc-11286928.title: Modifiable lifestyle factors and the risk of post-COVID-19 multisystem sequelae, hospitalization, and death
pmc-11286928.creator: Yunhe Wang, Binbin Su, Marta Alcalde-Herraiz, Nicola L Barclay, Yaohua Tian, Chunxiao Li, Nicholas J Wareham, Roger Paredes, Junqing Xie, Daniel Prieto-Alhambra
pmc-11286928.description: Effective prevention strategies for post-COVID complications are crucial for patients, clinicians, and policy makers to mitigate their cumulative burden. This study evaluated the association of modifiable lifestyle factors (smoking, alcohol intake, BMI, physical activity, sedentary time, sleep duration, and dietary habits) with COVID-19 multisystem sequelae, death, and hospitalization in the UK Biobank cohort (n = 68,896).

pmc-11440788.title: Embodied leisure experiences of nature-based activities for people living with dementia
pmc-11440788.creator: Steven Owen, Stephen Page, Katie Ledingham, Stephan Price, Joanne Connell, Catherine Quinn, Linda Clare
pmc-11440788.description: PurposeThis article adopts an embodiment lens to explore the individual leisure experiences of people living with dementia when engaging in nature-based pursuits. It focuses on how people living with dementia frame their everyday experiences of nature and how these are shaped by any cognitive challenges and/or other comorbidities affecting physical health.

pmc-11738799.title: The unique immune evasion mechanisms of the mpox virus and their implication for developing new vaccines and immunotherapies
pmc-11738799.creator: Dong Fang, Yan Liu, Dou Dou, Bin Su
pmc-11738799.description: Mpox is an infectious and contagious zoonotic disease caused by the mpox virus (MPXV), which belongs to the genus Orthopoxvirus. Since 2022, MPXV has posed a significant threat to global public health. The emergence of thousands of cases across the Western Hemisphere prompted the World Health Organization to declare an emergency.

pmc-12431022.title: FM-Net: A New Method for Detecting Smoke and Flames
pmc-12431022.creator: Jingwu Wang, Yuan Yao, Yinuo Huo, Jinfu Guan
pmc-12431022.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Aiming at the core problem of high false and missed alarm rate and insufficient interference resistance of existing smoke and fire detection algorithms in complex scenes, this paper proposes a target detection network based on improved feature pyramid structure.

pmc-12504559.title: Computational identification of PTPRJ peptide targeting the Epstein Barr virus latent membrane protein 1
pmc-12504559.creator: Dayang-Sharyati D A Salam, Hwang Siaw San, Xavier Chee Wezen
pmc-12504559.description: The treatment of Epstein-Barr virus (EBV)-associated malignancies is increasingly recognizing the necessity of personalized medicine strategies to enhance therapeutic outcomes. This research addresses this need by computationally investigating potential peptide inhibitors targeting the latent membrane protein 1 (LMP1), a key oncoprotein in EBV-related cancers.

pmc-12583653.title: Dapagliflozin ameliorates high glucose-induced peritoneal fibrosis through downregulation of ENKUR/PI3K/AKT signaling pathway

pmc-13053984.title: Transcriptomic analysis reveals a crucial role of the yolk sac during Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli infection in chicken embryos
pmc-13053984.creator: Jingyao Wang, Yadav Sharma Bajagai, Ghulam Asghar Sajid, Runsheng Li, Surya Paudel
pmc-13053984.description: Colibacillosis caused by Avian Pathogenic Escherichia coli (APEC) is a major threat to poultry, and yolk sac infection is a leading cause of embryonic mortality. However, the molecular mechanisms and host responses during the infection have not yet been investigated.

pmc-13499762.title: CT-based application of the Iscan method on isolated ribs: reliability, accuracy, and the role of joint fossa sclerosis in age estimation on a contemporary European skeletal sample
pmc-13499762.creator: Laura Filograna, Giulia Ceccobelli, Alessandro Mauro Tavone, Andrea Micillo, Raimondo Vella, Arianna D’Altorio, Flavia Chirico, Silvia Daria Beca, Alessandro Carini, Francesco Garaci, Maria Cristina Martinez-Labarga, Gian Luca Marella, Guglielmo Manenti
pmc-13499762.description: This study evaluates the applicability of the Iscan method to Post-Mortem Computed Tomography (PMCT) for age estimation through morphological analysis of the sternal end of the fourth right rib. Employing a double-blind design, two observers independently assessed a sample of 112 fragments of fourth ribs from individuals of European origin, isolated and processed before CT imaging.
